materials.title: Пищевая цепь и возвращение волков · B1
materials.text:
Teacher: What happens if wolves disappear?
Learner: Other animals can become more common, and some plants may disappear.
Teacher: Can putting the wolves back help?
Learner: It can help the plants recover and restore the balance.
Partner: Where did you find that in the article?
Learner: In the second paragraph. Let’s read that sentence again.

materials.title: Пищевая цепь и возвращение волков · B2
materials.text:
Teacher: Why are wolves important in the food web?
Learner: As top predators, they can influence how other animals behave. That can affect the vegetation further down the food web.
Partner: Would you call that a trophic cascade?
Learner: Yes. The reintroduction of one species can set off a chain reaction.
Teacher: Can you justify your answer with evidence from the text?
Learner: The author describes how vegetation had time to recover.

materials.title: Пищевая цепь и возвращение волков · C1
materials.text:
Teacher: Is the effect limited to the prey population?
Learner: The article links the reintroduction of wolves to changes in where prey feed, which may allow some vegetation to recover.
Partner: Does that prove that the wolves caused every change in the park?
Learner: I’d be cautious about that. The timing supports a link, but other influences may have played a part.
Teacher: Summarise it in one sentence.
Learner: Restoring a top predator can trigger a trophic cascade, with effects across the wider food web.

materials.title: Какой вид ты вернул бы · B1
materials.text:
Partner: If you could bring back one extinct animal, which would you choose?
Learner: I’d choose Steller’s sea cow. I’d like to see how it lived.
Partner: Where could it live now?
Learner: It would need a safe place to live and enough food.
Partner: What about animals that are in danger today?
Learner: We should protect them before they disappear.

materials.title: Какой вид ты вернул бы · B2
materials.text:
Teacher: Which extinct species would you bring back, and why?
Learner: I’d consider Steller’s sea cow, but only if we could provide a suitable habitat.
Partner: Could bringing it back affect other species?
Learner: It could. I’d want to know what it would eat and how the ecosystem has changed.
Teacher: What’s the alternative?
Learner: Invest in protecting endangered species that still have a chance to recover.

materials.title: Какой вид ты вернул бы · C1
materials.text:
Teacher: If bringing a species back were feasible, what would determine your choice?
Learner: I’d weigh the potential ecological benefits against the risk of unintended consequences. A species can return only if the conditions it needs still exist.
Partner: Would you prioritise a famous extinct species?
Learner: I’d be more inclined to restore the habitat of a species already under threat. We have a clearer idea of what it needs and more opportunities to intervene.

materials.title: Экодом и полезные технологии · B1
materials.text:
Partner: What would you change in your home?
Learner: I’d use better insulation and change the old light bulbs.
Partner: What about solar panels?
Learner: I’d like solar panels, but first I’d check whether the roof gets enough sun.
Partner: What can you do with rainwater?
Learner: You can collect it in a water butt and use it in the garden.

materials.title: Экодом и полезные технологии · B2
materials.text:
Teacher: How could a house be designed to use less energy?
Learner: I’d start with insulation and double glazing. A smart meter could show whether the changes actually reduce energy use.
Partner: Would you install underfloor heating as well?
Learner: It depends on the building. In an existing home, changing the thermostat and reducing heat loss might be more practical.
Teacher: Give an example of a sustainable material.
Learner: Builders could use locally sourced bamboo where it meets the design requirements.

materials.title: Экодом и полезные технологии · C1
materials.text:
Teacher: Which improvements would you prioritise if the budget were limited?
Learner: I’d start by locating the main sources of heat loss, then upgrade insulation or glazing where it would have the biggest impact.
Partner: Would you invest in a smart shower or solar panels straight away?
Learner: I’d compare the upfront cost with the potential savings. A smart shower could cut water use, while the value of solar panels would depend on the roof and local conditions.
Teacher: What is your principle?
Learner: Measure actual consumption, address avoidable losses, then decide which equipment is worth installing.

materials.title: В малой группе: уточнить и обосновать · B1
materials.text:
Partner: What did you put for number three?
Learner: I put underfloor heating.
Partner: Why?
Learner: It heats the room from below the floor.
Partner: And number four?
Learner: An energy-efficient light bulb. Could you send me the picture again?

materials.title: В малой группе: уточнить и обосновать · B2
materials.text:
Partner: Can we compare our answers before we go back?
Learner: Sure. For number three I put underfloor heating, because the clue refers to heat rising from the floor.
Partner: What did you put for number four?
Learner: An energy-efficient light bulb. I missed number five. Could you read the clue out loud?
Partner: I think it refers to collecting rainwater.
Learner: Then a water butt makes sense.

materials.title: В малой группе: уточнить и обосновать · C1
materials.text:
Partner: How did you distinguish the thermostat from the smart meter?
Learner: The key distinction is that a thermostat regulates temperature, whereas a smart meter measures energy use.
Partner: The clue for the next one could mean two things.
Learner: Could you read it word for word? Let’s check which interpretation the wording actually supports.
Partner: Shall we take our answer back to the main room?
Learner: Yes. Let’s explain the reasoning as well as giving the answer.

materials.title: Радиоинтервью: первое и второе прослушивание · B1
materials.text:
Teacher: What is the interview about?
Learner: It’s about a man who wants to use less energy at home.
Teacher: Why did he start making changes?
Learner: His first energy bill was much higher than he expected.
Teacher: What does his new shower do?
Learner: It switches off automatically to save water.

materials.title: Радиоинтервью: первое и второе прослушивание · B2
materials.text:
Teacher: What did you get from the first listen?
Learner: The speaker started with simple changes after receiving a surprisingly high bill. Later he installed equipment that reduced energy and water use.
Partner: What detail did you miss?
Learner: I heard the part about a smart fridge, but I missed the exact figure for the solar panels. Could we listen to that section again?
Teacher: What does the fridge do?
Learner: It suggests meals based on the food he already has, so he throws less away.

materials.title: Радиоинтервью: первое и второе прослушивание · C1
materials.text:
Teacher: How would you separate the main argument from the examples?
Learner: The main point is that a high bill prompted the speaker to examine how his household used energy. The bulbs, solar panels and shower illustrate different ways of reducing waste.
Partner: How certain are you about the figures?
Learner: I’d verify those on the second listen. I’m confident about the reason for the changes, but not about the proportion of electricity the panels supply.

materials.title: Причина → результат
materials.prompt: Объясни эффект реинтродукции волков в трёх предложениях. Используй lead to, as a result и trophic cascade.
materials.answer: Reintroducing wolves can lead to changes in the behaviour of other animals. As a result, some vegetation may recover. This kind of chain reaction is called a trophic cascade.

materials.title: Четыре предмета экодома
materials.prompt: Объясни разницу между thermostat, smart meter, insulation и double glazing. Для каждого дай пример.
materials.answer: A thermostat controls the temperature. A smart meter measures energy use. Insulation slows heat loss. Double glazing uses two panes of glass to reduce heat loss through windows.

materials.title: Выбор с оговоркой
materials.prompt: Предложи одно экологическое улучшение и назови возможный минус. Затем спроси партнёра, согласен ли он.
materials.answer: I'd improve the insulation first because it could cut heat loss and reduce energy bills. The drawback is the upfront cost. Would you make the same choice?

materials.title: Аудирование: уверен / нужно проверить
materials.prompt: Прочитай пересказ интервью. Назови одну деталь, которую можешь объяснить, и одну, для которой попросишь повторить аудио.
materials.answer: I’m confident that the high bill prompted him to make changes. I’d like to listen again to check the exact figure for electricity generated by the solar panels.

1. Wolves began to disappear because they ran out of elk to hunt.
2. The rise in elk numbers affected the rest of the ecosystem.
3. The elk population grew because wolves returned.
4. The article says returning wolves helped improve the health of the elk population.
5. More types of plants grew again as wolf numbers increased.
6. Plant regrowth contributed to the rivers becoming deeper.
materials.answer:
1 False — the article says wolves were hunted.
2 True — the expanding elk population affected the wider ecosystem.
3 False — wolves slowed the expansion of the elk population.
4 True — the article links predation to the overall health of the elk population.
5 True — native plants had time to recover.
6 True — the article associates regrowth with stronger riverbanks and deeper rivers.
Это ключ к тексту урока. Для осторожного пересказа используй the article suggests / links X to Y.

materials.title: Реплики преподавателя · 12 фраз с переводом и примерами
materials.text:
Таймкоды от начала файла, в формате часы:минуты. Фразы сверены с расшифровкой и местами нормализованы, чтобы их было удобно повторять. Примеры после каждой фразы составлены для практики.

00:06–00:08 · You’ve got the main idea.
Перевод: Ты уловил основную мысль.
Конструкция: get the main idea — понять суть
Твой пример для практики: I think I’ve got the main idea. Could we check the details now?

00:06–00:08 · Could you share your opinion?
Перевод: Можешь поделиться мнением?
Конструкция: could you + глагол; share your opinion
Твой пример для практики: Could you share your opinion on the two options?

00:06–00:08 · Let’s read the article again and look for more details.
Перевод: Давай перечитаем статью и найдём больше подробностей.
Конструкция: look for + что ищем; look at + куда смотрим
Твой пример для практики: Let’s look for evidence in the second paragraph.

00:16–00:18 · Let’s check them one by one.
Перевод: Давай проверим их по очереди.
Конструкция: one by one — по одному, последовательно
Твой пример для практики: Let’s go through your questions one by one.

00:16–00:20 · Can you tell me where we can find the answer?
Перевод: Можешь сказать, где найти ответ?
Конструкция: В косвенном вопросе порядок where + we + can.
Твой пример для практики: Could you tell me where I can find the slides?

00:20–00:22 · Let’s find the evidence in these two paragraphs.
Перевод: Давай найдём подтверждение в этих двух абзацах.
Конструкция: evidence неисчисляемое: some evidence, a piece of evidence
Твой пример для практики: I found some evidence in the second paragraph.

00:20–00:22 · Your answer is right, and you found the evidence.
Перевод: Твой ответ верный, и ты нашёл подтверждение.
Конструкция: right — верный; support an answer — подкрепить ответ
Твой пример для практики: I think it’s true. This sentence supports my answer.

01:04–01:06 · Is it the same as a thermometer?
Перевод: Это то же самое, что термометр?
Конструкция: the same as, different from
Твой пример для практики: Is a smart meter the same as a thermostat?

01:04–01:06 · How many syllables are there? Where is the stress?
Перевод: Сколько слогов? Где ударение?
Конструкция: syllable — слог; the stress is on the first syllable
Твой пример для практики: There are three syllables. The stress is on the first one.

01:12–01:14 · Does it measure the energy we use?
Перевод: Он измеряет, сколько энергии мы используем?
Конструкция: После does идёт основная форма measure.
Твой пример для практики: Does the meter show how much electricity we use?

01:54–01:56 · Listen for gist and then listen for detail.
Перевод: Сначала слушай, чтобы уловить суть, затем — детали.
Конструкция: listen for + что пытаемся услышать; listen to + источник
Твой пример для практики: I listened to the interview for gist first.

01:54–01:56 · Share your ideas with your partner and give reasons.
Перевод: Поделись идеями с партнёром и обоснуй их.
Конструкция: share X with Y; give a reason for + существительное/-ing
Твой пример для практики: I’d start with insulation. My main reason is heat loss.

materials.title: Грамматика урока · правила, формы и примеры
materials.text:
Вежливые и косвенные вопросы
Прямой вопрос: Where can I find the answer? Вежливая рамка: Could you tell me where I can find the answer? Внутри рамки ставь подлежащее перед глаголом. Без вопросительного слова используй if или whether: Could you tell me whether the roof gets enough sun?

Причина и результат
Lead to / bring about + существительное: The return of wolves led to changes in elk behaviour. As a result, + отдельное предложение. As a result of + существительное или -ing: As a result of the changes, some vegetation recovered. Which in turn + глагол показывает следующий эффект: The plants recovered, which in turn strengthened the riverbanks. Если пересказываешь статью, отделяй её вывод от своего: The article links X to Y.

Неисчисляемые слова
Evidence, insulation и equipment в этом контексте неисчисляемые. Употребляй some evidence, better insulation, a piece of equipment. Но a thermostat, two smart meters, an energy-efficient light bulb можно считать. Дефис в energy-efficient light bulb связывает слова в определении перед существительным.

Более раннее прошлое и пассив
The plants had been eaten before they began to recover. Had + been + past participle ставит более раннее действие в прошедшем на первый план, а plants обозначает объект действия. The plants had been eaten by elk — если важен исполнитель. The plants recovered — обычный Past Simple для следующего события.

Установка, которую выполняет кто-то другой
We’re having a smart meter installed. Have/get + предмет + причастие: попросить или организовать, чтобы работу выполнили. Сравни We’re installing a meter (в контексте можем устанавливать сами) и We’re having a meter installed (организуем установку). Этот пример из учебного радиоинтервью, около 02:20–02:22.
